about: Reading faces over the 250,000-byte gzipped budget, each held to its measured size (scripts/perf/readingFaces.ts, row reading-face-html of scripts/run-perf-budgets.ts). A recorded face fails when it grows past its size; an unrecorded face fails over 250,000. The budget is not raised. First measured on a build of 54c8cbf4 on 2026-09-26; relativity's German, English and parallel faces and light quanta's parallel face re-measured on a build of 9f3c915d the same day, gzip level 9, the random build id blanked (dispatch 254); light quanta's parallel face re-measured on a build of f27080a9 the same day, after its inline formulas were drawn in colour (dispatch 272); relativity's German, English, parallel and results faces re-measured on builds of 61f173a7 with and without dispatch 277's change, after its inline formulas were drawn in colour. WIDENED 2026-09-29 (dispatch 469): the row walked three URL shapes and measured 60 of the 257 pages under out/papers; it now walks the tree. The 23 faces recorded with that date were over the budget before the row could see them, so the count rose because the measurement did, not because the site did. Each is held to the size measured on the 21:22 build. WHAT MAKES THEM LARGE, measured 2026-09-29 by attributing every byte of special-relativity/s3/view/parallel/index.html with an HTML parser (dispatch 472): 64.2% of its 6.96 MB is React's hydration flight payload inside <script>, 21.1% is KaTeX HTML, 11.6% is prose and chrome, 3.1% is MathML. Priced marginally by removing a kind and recompressing, the payload is 266.6 kB of the 417.3 kB gzipped, and the page without it is 152.9 kB, under the budget with 91 kB to spare. It carries the same content a second time: katex-html appears 1,439 times in the rendered markup and 1,824 times in the payload, frac-line 386 and 386, and a sample prose sentence 3 and 3. THE FOUR READINGS ARE NOT THE CAUSE and AGENTS.md's R2/R3-fragment remedy does not address this: data-detail appears ZERO times on both over-budget pages and 8 times on the whole paper's page. brownian-motion/s4 has the same profile at 59.1% payload, and so does the whole relativity paper at 63.6%, so this is the site's shape rather than these pages'. WHICH COMPONENT IS HANDED IT, measured by decoding the flight stream of that page (dispatch 475): 1,464 push calls, 3,313,815 characters, 23 client components declared, 974,505 characters of decoded client props. BlockTermChips is 812,435 of those characters, 83%, across 124 instances, one per block, whose `items` prop averages 6,711 characters and peaks at 33,375. TermHighlight is another 124 instances at 77,266, and InlineTermLighting one instance carrying a 72,581-character `quantities` map. The items repeat: 780 records serialised, 61 distinct, speedOfLight 94 times and frameSpeed 93, so 91% of that prop is the same 61 records again, and a third of its bytes are glyphHtml, KaTeX markup the page also renders. REDUCIBLE IN PART, AND THE COMPRESSED NUMBER IS SMALLER THAN THE RAW ONE SUGGESTS: rewriting those 124 lists as one catalogue plus ids shrinks the stream 22% and the page by 44.2 kB gzipped, 417.3 to about 373, which is still 129 kB over budget because gzip was already collapsing the repetition. The rest is the cost of hydrating a page whose content is 28,449 KaTeX elements; the page without its flight payload is 152.9 kB, under budget. Whether those 124 blocks need hydrating is a design question for the owner, not a prop trim. THE OPTIONS PRICED (dispatch 477), each by rewriting the flight stream and recompressing, on special-relativity/s3/view/parallel/ at 417.3 kB against a 244.1 KiB budget: one catalogue plus ids saves 44.2 kB; ids only with no glyph 51.0; ids and names 48.2; not hydrating BlockTermChips at all 54.2. Removing EVERY client component from that stream saves 70.9 kB and leaves the page at 346.4, still 102 kB over, while removing the whole flight payload saves 264.4 and leaves it at 152.9, under. So the client components are 71 kB of a 264 kB payload and the other 194 kB is the serialisation of the server-rendered tree itself: no change to what BlockTermChips is handed, and no decision about hydrating it, can close this gap. The same holds on brownian-motion/s4, where every client component is 36.0 kB of a 162.6 kB payload. THE SHAPE IS SYSTEMIC BUT THE COMPONENT IS NOT: on light-quanta's parallel face BlockTermChips is 468,775 of 651,686 characters of props, 72%, as on s3; on brownian-motion/s4, a section index rather than a parallel face, the largest is SemanticEquation at 149,281 characters over 14 instances, each handed a whole equation record. A client component given an entire content record is the pattern; which component it is depends on the face. ALL 28 BROKEN DOWN (dispatch 479): script 59.1% to 65.2% with a median of 64.9%, KaTeX 18.7% to 22.9%, prose and chrome 9.0% to 17.8%, MathML 2.4% to 3.6%. ZERO faces fall outside the band s3 (64.2%) and s4 (59.1%) sit in, so none of the 23 is over budget for a different reason and the tree serialisation is the story everywhere. BUT THE UNIFORM SPLIT HIDES A SECOND DEFECT, which is visible only in the sizes: relativity's eleven section English faces are 343.5 to 343.7 kB, within 200 bytes of each other AND of the whole paper's English face, because each carries the WHOLE paper's English text: 106,302 to 106,325 visible characters against the whole paper's 106,333, a spread of 0.02%. The parallel faces are partly scoped by comparison, at 51% to 59% of the whole paper's text, so the German half varies with the section and the English half does not. That is a content-scoping defect rather than a payload one, it is invisible in a percentage split because every page has the same shape, and it is the larger lever: a section English face scoped to its own section would be a fraction of 250,000 bytes, which would take eleven of these twenty-three records off this list without touching hydration at all. AND IT WAS DONE, so this list is now six records rather than twenty-three (dispatch 484). Measured with the same instrument on a build begun at 341d07f6 on 2026-09-29 (the dates in this file are UTC; that build ran on the evening of 2026-09-28 local, and HEAD had moved to b84aace1 by the time it finished, because a build compiles the working tree while peers commit into it). The section English faces were scoped in 4a3f676c and the section parallel faces in 341d07f6: the English face rendered every unit in the paper, and the parallel face scoped its German half by filtering blocks while its English half ran over every unit, so parallelRows, which gives an English group whose German block a page does not print a row of its own, printed the other nine sections. TWENTY-TWO OF THE TWENTY-EIGHT RECORDS ARE REMOVED, not lowered: relativity's eleven section parallel faces fell from 363,762-427,342 to 41,163-162,793 bytes and its eleven section English faces from 351,751-351,971 to 31,688-92,671, so every one is under the 250,000-byte budget and owes nothing. A record describes a debt, and a face with no debt needs none; leaving a record at a lowered ceiling would leave a budget to draw on, and removing it holds the face to the budget itself, which is stricter. Over the whole tree the row now reports SIX faces over budget out of 256, against 23 of 224 on the 21:22 build. THE SIX THAT REMAIN are relativity's whole-paper German, English, parallel and results faces, light quanta's whole-paper parallel face, and brownian-motion/s4, which is a section index rather than a reading face. The five whole-paper faces are supposed to carry a whole paper (TanElk, mail 40857), so what they owe is the payload shape described above rather than a scoping defect, and none of the options priced above closes it. THEIR CEILINGS ARE NOT RAISED although all six measured 42 to 1,110 bytes above them on this build, inside the 2,048-byte allowance: a baseline that only ever rises is a budget. THE OTHER FACES WERE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, through the page component on relativity: the section German faces carry 4% to 19% of the whole paper's visible text and the section results faces 6% to 20%, so both were already scoped, and the gloss prints its own section while the whole-paper gloss page prints the first section and links the rest, which is why that page is the small one. The split face is a chooser holding two real links, 566 visible characters by design.

faces.reason: The whole German text of relativity, 31 printed pages, with 98 coloured printed displays and their term chips. React's flight data carries the page's element tree a second time for hydration: 182 kB of the 305 kB measured on live 0c6777c7. TanElk ruled (mail 40857) that the reading faces stay whole-paper, for find-in-page across the paper, and are not cut. Was 352933; re-measured on a build of 9f3c915d on 2026-09-26 (TanElk), after reader features that add weight to the German, English and parallel faces: the three German faces on their source blocks (8b1cbcb8), the printed page turns marked in the text (7f464ab8), footnotes opening with their printed marks (e857018e), the 1905 misprints marked (288332c9, 9c6500bf) and noted under their displays (9f8f278f), and the period-word notes (943e59da, 5f9aaaec, 73a0563a). Recorded at the measured size rather than cut, since each is text or navigation a reader uses; the budget is not raised. It measured 367,606 on a build of 61f173a7 and 385,289 on the same commit with dispatch 277's change, which draws its inline formulas in the paper's colours (the owner's request). Of the 17,683 bytes, measured by removing each part from the built page: about 6,004 are the inspector's facts for the quantities the inline formulas name, one copy per page; about 3,459 KaTeX's wrapper and ids around each coloured glyph; about 1,674 the marks on each formula's span; about 2,185 the facts, with their modern letters, that the 28 new concordance entries give the displays' inspectors; the rest, about 4,361, is not separated. None of it is text. Re-measured on a build of af0f86e3 on 2026-09-27, after "Explain this equation" landed under every printed display. Inlining every level of every explanation had taken this face to 854,623; dd7bd466 moved the levels a reader has not opened into a fragment fetched on first expansion, and what remains on the face is one link per equation. Recorded because the growth is that link, measured at 3.2 per cent, not text that could be cut.
